name: URINE PROTEIN
description: Urine Protein measures total protein in urine to detect proteinuria. This test screens for renal disease, preeclampsia, and other protein-losing conditions.
literatureReview: Urine Protein detects proteinuria using tetrabromophenol blue indicator. Normal: negative or trace. Abnormal: 1+, 2+, 3+, 4+. Semi-quantitative assessment. More sensitive to albumin than globulins. False positives with alkaline urine, quaternary ammonium compounds, or detergents. False negatives with dilute urine or non-albumin proteins. Positive result requires 24-hour urine protein quantification. Used in screening for glomerulonephritis, diabetic nephropathy, preeclampsia, multiple myeloma, and urinary tract infections. Critical marker for renal function assessment.
